newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Sears to expand home shopping.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Sears to expand home shopping.

text.p: Retail group Sears Plc is looking to expand its home shopping business and wants to develop the direct mail order side, based on its retail brands such as Selfridges, Wallis and Adams.
Chief executive Liam Strong said the group was committed to home shopping for the long term.
"We feel that if we were able to find the right way to expand we would do so," he said in a telephone interview.
The group would not rule out acquisitions, he said.

Strong said the direct side of the business -- catalogues which have no sales agents -- grew by 44 percent in the first half. But Freemans, Sears main mail order business, saw sales fall 6.5 percent to 237.0 million stg.

Strong blamed failure to recruit enough agents in 1995 on the poor performance from Freemans. But he said recruitment was up five percent in the first half and about 13 percent up in the year to date.
He said this would improve Freemans performance, but not in the near term as it would take new agents time to become productive.
"It takes about a year to become really fully productive, so we're really being cautious until those agents come on stream," he said.

Sears' department store Selfridges produced another strong performance with profits up by 21.8 percent to 13.4 million stg. The group plans to open a new store in Manchester in 1998 and is looking to opening a further three or four regional stores by 2000.
Selfridges in London's main shopping district, Oxford Street, could gain an extra 200,000 square feet of space if current development plans go ahead.

Strong said Sears had no plans to buy other department stores. "There are no plans to buy other department stores at this point in time. We feel we have enough scope within Selfridges without buying anything else."
He said the group had completed the rationalisation of British Shoe and that there would be no need for further provisions.

The group has sold 149 of the stores out of 379 it had to take back from Facia, the retail empire which collapsed earlier this year. There were 85 under offer, leaving 145 still to be sold, Strong said.
He said Sears had reorganised behind the scenes operations such as finance and personnel, which would bring savings of eight million stg next year and 22 million stg by 2000.
He said net debt at the half year was 18 million stg, but the group would have net cash by the year-end after disposals were completed.
"We are looking for a steady improvement in performance from now on," Strong said.
